issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for class Animal: the UML in problem_statement.md declares a constructor 'Animal(String, int)' (name and age) but the solution's Animal.java defines a single-argument constructor 'Animal(String)'. Template/Main.java example usages (Seal, Pig, Goat) also use single-argument constructors. This inconsistency leaves students uncertain whether to implement a two-parameter constructor (and update all subclasses) or a single-parameter one, and may cause compilation/value-mismatch if assignment expectations differ.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across the specification, template examples, and solution. Either (A) update problem_statement.md and the UML to require only Animal(String) (remove the age parameter), or (B) change the solution and template to implement Animal(String, int) and update all subclass constructors (Seal, Pig, Goat) and example usages in Main.java to pass both name and age, plus add corresponding getters/setters for age.

issues.description: Attribute mismatch for class Animal: the UML in problem_statement.md lists attributes 'name: String' and 'age: int', but solution's Animal.java declares only a 'name' attribute (no 'age' field). This discrepancy confuses students about required fields to implement and initialize and whether tests or further tasks expect an 'age' field.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the class attributes between the UML/specification and the implementation. Either (A) add an 'age' (int) field to Animal.java with corresponding constructor parameter(s), getter and setter, and update subclasses and example usages; or (B) remove the 'age' attribute from the UML/problem statement so the spec matches the intended simple design that uses only a name.
